author: Karl Rock
description:
Why are the mysterious Chaukhandi Tombs in Pakistan covered in intricate carvings of jewellery, weapons and horses? Let's explore one of the country's most fascinating and least-visited historical sites.

Join me as I explore the remarkable Chaukhandi (also spelled Chaukundi) Tombs near Karachi, Sindh, one of Pakistan's most fascinating yet least-visited historical sites. These beautifully carved sandstone tombs date from the 15th to 18th centuries and are renowned for their intricate geometric patterns and symbolic carvings that reveal clues about the people buried beneath them.

The Chaukhandi Tombs are considered some of the finest examples of carved sandstone funerary architecture in Pakistan. Built from carefully stacked buff sandstone, the tombs feature beautifully detailed carvings depicting jewellery, weapons, horses, floral motifs and geometric designs.
